title: 2014 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by reversing its digits is \(5\) times the sum of the digits of either number. What is the sum of the two-digit number and its reverse?

solutions.text:
Let the larger number be \(10a+b.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} &(10a+b)-(10b+a)=9(a-b)\\ &\quad{}=5(a+b), \end{aligned} \] which simplifies to \(2a=7b.\)

The only nonzero digits satisfying this are \(a=7\) and \(b=2,\) so the number is \(72\) and its reverse is \(27.\)

Their sum is \(72+27=99.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the number as \(10a+b\) and its reverse as \(10b+a\)
The difference is \(9(a-b)\), and setting it equal to \(5(a+b)\) gives \(2a=7b\)
